Observed Hill numbers

Source: R/alpha.R
div_hill.Rd

Computes Hill numbers of order q for each site from the observed relative abundances. Order 0 is species richness, order 1 is the exponential of Shannon entropy and order 2 is the inverse Simpson index.

Usage

div_hill(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  type = c("TD", "PD", "FD"),
  tree = NULL,
  reftime = NULL,
  pd_unit = c("mean", "total"),
  distance = NULL,
  tau = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

q

Orders of diversity, non-negative numbers.

type

Diversity dimension: "TD" (taxonomic, the default), "PD" (phylogenetic, needs tree) or "FD" (functional, needs distance). Give several, such as c("TD", "PD"), or "all" for all three, to analyse the dimensions together: the results are stacked in one tibble with a type column, and autoplot() shows them side by side. All three are Hill numbers of the same order q, in units of effective numbers of species (Chao, Chiu and Jost 2014), and reproduce iNEXT.3D.

tree

For type = "PD", a rooted ape::phylo tree with branch lengths whose tip labels include every species.

reftime

For type = "PD", the reference time (tree depth) at which diversity is measured. Defaults to the age of the root of the tree pruned to the species in data.

pd_unit

For type = "PD", "mean" (the default) divides phylogenetic diversity by reftime, giving the effective number of lineages on the same scale as species; "total" gives effective total branch length.

distance

For type = "FD", a species-by-species distance matrix (or stats::dist object) with names matching the species, scaled to lie between 0 and 1, for example from Gower distances of traits.

tau

For type = "FD", the distance threshold below which species are treated as functionally identical. Defaults to the mean distance between two individuals in the pooled data. Use "auc" to integrate over all thresholds from 0 to 1 (Chao et al. 2019).

unit

For incidence data, the column naming the sampling unit (a trap, bait, plot or survey day) in which each species was detected. Each site is then described by the number of units in which each species was found and the number of units sampled, and every estimate is incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014), for TD, PD and FD alike. Leave NULL for abundance data.

n_units

For incidence data, a column giving the number of units sampled at each site, constant within a site. Use it when some units detected no species and so do not appear in the data. By default the number of distinct units in the data is used.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A tibble with the grouping columns, the site column, q, n (number of individuals, or of sampling units for incidence data) and diversity. Phylogenetic and functional results also have type and reftime or tau.

References

Hill, M. O. (1973). Diversity and evenness: a unifying notation and its consequences. Ecology, 54, 427-432. doi:10.2307/1934352

Chao, A., Chiu, C.-H. and Jost, L. (2014). Unifying species diversity, phylogenetic diversity, functional diversity, and related similarity and differentiation measures through Hill numbers. Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics, 45, 297-324. doi:10.1146/annurev-ecolsys-120213-091540

Chao, A., Chiu, C.-H., Villeger, S., Sun, I.-F., Thorn, S., Lin, Y.-C., Chiang, J.-M. and Sherwin, W. B. (2019). An attribute-diversity approach to functional diversity, functional beta diversity, and related (dis)similarity measures. Ecological Monographs, 89, e01343. doi:10.1002/ecm.1343

Examples

div_hill(png_ants, .by = season)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 5
#>    season site       q     n diversity
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200     0    47     16   
#>  2 dry    MW0200     1    47     12.3 
#>  3 dry    MW0200     2    47      9.91
#>  4 dry    MW0700     0    23     15   
#>  5 dry    MW0700     1    23     11.8 
#>  6 dry    MW0700     2    23      8.67
#>  7 dry    MW1200     0    29     13   
#>  8 dry    MW1200     1    29      9.37
#>  9 dry    MW1200     2    29      6.73
#> 10 dry    MW1700     0    17      5   
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# Grouped data frames work too
png_ants |>
  dplyr::group_by(season) |>
  div_hill(q = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2))
#> # A tibble: 40 × 5
#>    season site       q     n diversity
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200   0      47     16   
#>  2 dry    MW0200   0.5    47     14.0 
#>  3 dry    MW0200   1      47     12.3 
#>  4 dry    MW0200   2      47      9.91
#>  5 dry    MW0700   0      23     15   
#>  6 dry    MW0700   0.5    23     13.5 
#>  7 dry    MW0700   1      23     11.8 
#>  8 dry    MW0700   2      23      8.67
#>  9 dry    MW1200   0      29     13   
#> 10 dry    MW1200   0.5    29     11.1 
#> # ℹ 30 more rows

# Incidence data: each bait is a sampling unit, 60 baits per site
div_hill(png_ants, unit = bait, n_units = baits, .by = season)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 5
#>    season site       q     n diversity
#>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> <int>     <dbl>
#>  1 dry    MW0200     0    60     16   
#>  2 dry    MW0200     1    60     12.3 
#>  3 dry    MW0200     2    60      9.91
#>  4 dry    MW0700     0    60     15   
#>  5 dry    MW0700     1    60     11.8 
#>  6 dry    MW0700     2    60      8.67
#>  7 dry    MW1200     0    60     13   
#>  8 dry    MW1200     1    60      9.37
#>  9 dry    MW1200     2    60      6.73
#> 10 dry    MW1700     0    60      5   
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# TD, PD and FD together, here for a functional distance matrix only
d <- as.matrix(stats::dist(c(s1 = 0, s2 = 0.1, s3 = 0.5, s4 = 1)))
toy <- data.frame(
  site = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4), species = paste0("s", 1:4),
  n = c(10, 5, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1)
)
div_hill(toy, abundance = n, type = c("TD", "FD"), distance = d)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 6
#>    site      q     n diversity type     tau
#>    <chr> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <fct>  <dbl>
#>  1 a         0    18      4    TD    NA    
#>  2 a         1    18      2.97 TD    NA    
#>  3 a         2    18      2.49 TD    NA    
#>  4 b         0     8      4    TD    NA    
#>  5 b         1     8      3.51 TD    NA    
#>  6 b         2     8      3.2  TD    NA    
#>  7 a         0    18      3.23 FD     0.245
#>  8 a         1    18      2.07 FD     0.245
#>  9 a         2    18      1.71 FD     0.245
#> 10 b         0     8      3.26 FD     0.245
#> 11 b         1     8      2.48 FD     0.245
#> 12 b         2     8      2.09 FD     0.245
